sourceNote: Transcribed from supplied exam screenshots; the original paper did not show an exam duration in those screenshots.

questions.text: QUESTION 1 (20 marks): In the Project Vision business case, correlate the needs of Project Vision's end-users (students with visual impairments) with ALL FIVE levels of Maslow's hierarchy of needs. Give a specific Project Vision example for each level. (5 × 4 marks.)
questions.correctAnswer: 1. Physiological (4): reliable access to transport and facilities enables Noma and other students to attend teaching, obtain basic necessities (including food/water/rest) and sustain everyday living. 2. Safety (4): certified drivers, safe door-to-door assistance, real-time ride updates, TWO EYES obstacle recognition and corridor/stairway navigation increase physical security and predictability. 3. Social/belonging (4): attending face-to-face/hybrid classes lets visually impaired students interact with classmates and teachers and participate in the campus community rather than being isolated by transport barriers. 4. Esteem (4): independence in travelling, studying and navigating campus builds confidence, self-respect, achievement and recognition, and lets students be treated as capable participants. 5. Self-actualisation (4): full engagement with Honours or other educational goals, learning, innovation and personal potential becomes possible when accessibility barriers are reduced. Accept other clear, case-linked examples at each of the correct five Maslow levels.
aiRubric: 4 marks for an accurate, specific Project Vision link to PHYSIOLOGICAL needs, not simply naming a level.
4 marks for SAFETY: trained drivers, safe travel, TWO EYES obstacle detection, safe navigation or equivalent.
4 marks for SOCIAL/BELONGING: attendance, inclusion, interaction, friendship/community.
4 marks for ESTEEM: autonomy, confidence, recognition, competence or achievement.
4 marks for SELF-ACTUALISATION: personal growth, studying to full potential, creativity and achievement.
Give partial credit per level for correct definition and a relevant case-study explanation. Do not confuse disability itself with the physiological-needs level.
questions.aiReferenceNotes: Award partial marks for clearly demonstrated method, valid working, sound case-study application and equivalent mathematically correct forms. Do not demand verbatim wording; allow reasonable rounding. Never award full marks when the key reasoning or calculation is missing.
questions.context:
PROJECT VISION CASE STUDY (INF3708 January/February 2025 supplementary examination)

Noma Nkosi, a 20-year-old visually impaired second-year BSc Computing student at the University of South Africa (Unisa), participated in Project Six Spoken Breaths until the end of 2024. The School of Computing initiative developed an AI tool to assist visually impaired students. The tool, TWO AUDIRE, is housed in purpose-built air pods with a powerful microprocessor.

TWO AUDIRE facilitates interaction with coursework and assessments using automatic speech recognition and natural language processing. It connects to module sites, the Internet and a virtual word-processing application that converts spoken responses to text. Noma can ask TWO AUDIRE to read assessment instructions, dictate answers, convert the result to a PDF and submit it via the assessment portal. The machine-learning system is not designed to provide verbatim answers to assessment questions, supporting academic honesty.

Noma wants an immersive experience of hybrid classes, including Dr Emil Van Der Poll's face-to-face classes on Mondays and Wednesdays, 18:30–20:30 at Florida Campus. Sessions are streamed and recorded using three cameras, but unreliable transportation prevents her from attending on campus.

Inspired by Bolt for Women, she conceptualised Bolt Vision, a ride-hailing service for visually impaired students. With assistance from TWO AUDIRE, riders could travel between home and campus. Noma and School of Computing academics drafted a business case for Project Vision: integrating TWO AUDIRE into the Bolt e-hailing app. Features include (1) natural conversations to request rides exclusively from certified Bolt Vision drivers; (2) communicating driver ratings; (3) payments; (4) live updates on pickup and drop-off times and distances; and (5) in-app calls between rider and driver.

Bolt Vision drivers, who may also serve regular customers, are trained and certified to assist visually impaired students. They guide the student from home to the car and escort the student to a campus-building entrance. Corridors and stairs remain a safety challenge because students can bump into staff and other students. Lead programmer Khushi Singh proposed TWO EYES: a camera and motion-detection feature to recognise obstacles and guide safe navigation. Its camera technology would be installed in smart glasses.

At the beginning of this academic year, you enrolled for Honours Information Systems. For the Software Project Management (INF4825) module you are Project Vision's PART-TIME project manager, only working hours allocated to the module.

questions.text: QUESTION 2.1 (2 marks): Your Project Vision labour rate is R120/hour. Full-time work would average 160 hours per month. Explain WHY the Project Manager's hours in Table 1 are divided by 2 in the calculation (160 ÷ 2) × 10 months = 800 hours.
questions.correctAnswer: The project manager only works PART-TIME on Project Vision, as described in the case study. Assuming half of a full-time monthly workload, 160/2 = 80 hours/month; across 10 months this is 80 × 10 = 800 hours. This is not 800 per month.
aiRubric: 1 mark: identify that the manager is assigned PART-TIME, not full-time.
1 mark: explain half of 160 = 80 hours per month; multiply by 10 = 800 total hours.

questions.text: QUESTION 2.7.1 (10 marks): Using the cash flows in Table 3, calculate Project Vision's payback period to the closest approximate YEAR, MONTH and DAY. Show annual cumulative cash flows and the fractional-year calculation.
questions.correctAnswer: Year 0 initial cost R3 477 840. Annual inflows years 1–4: R480 000 + R650 000 + R799 000 + R970 000 = R2 899 000. Amount unrecovered at end of year 4 = R3 477 840 − R2 899 000 = R578 840. Year 5 inflow = R1 220 000, so payback occurs during year 5. Fraction of year 5 = 578 840 / 1 220 000 = 0.474459 year. Total payback period = 4.474459 years ≈ 4 years, 5 months and 21 days using 12 months/year and 30 days/month (0.474459×12=5.69351 months; 0.69351×30≈20.81 days). A 365-day calendar convention gives approximately 4 years and 173 days, or about 4 years, 5 months and 22–23 days depending on month lengths. Accept clearly stated consistent approximation conventions.
aiRubric: 1 mark: identify initial negative cash flow R3 477 840.
Up to 4 marks: correctly sum annual inflows/cumulative cash flow through years 1–4 (R480k; R1.13m; R1.929m; R2.899m).
1 mark: outstanding balance after year 4 = R578 840.
1 mark: recognise payback takes place during YEAR 5 and use year 5 inflow R1 220 000.
1 mark: express result as approximately 4.47446 years / 4 years plus a year fraction.
1 mark: convert to ~5 months and 21 days with a disclosed 30-day month; accept other internally consistent day/month conventions.
Accept minor rounding differences and transparent alternative methods.
questions.aiReferenceNotes: Use the screenshot's Table 3 amounts. Payback: 4 + (R3 477 840 − R2 899 000)/R1 220 000 = 4.474459 years; ~4 years 5 months 21 days (30-day month method). The student earns marks for method even if a subsequent arithmetic slip changes their final number. Do not use discounted payback; no discount rate is requested.

questions.text: QUESTION 3.1 (24 marks; 12 × 2): Create an ACTIVITY-ON-NODE (AoN) network diagram of activities A–J in Table 4. Add separate START and END nodes (12 nodes in total). Follow Figure 2's node legend: earliest start (top-left), earliest finish (top-right), activity label and duration (centre), latest start (bottom-left), FREE SLACK (bottom-centre), and latest finish (bottom-right). Draw the diagram or upload a legible image; optional written calculations can support it.
questions.correctAnswer: Correct AoN precedence: START→A; A→B and E; B→C and D; E→F→G; C, D and G all precede H; H→I→J→END. Durations (weeks): A2 B3 C2 D2 E4 F3 G3 H2 I4 J1. Project duration 19 weeks. Correct node values as ES/EF/LS/LF, TOTAL float and FREE float respectively: A 0/2/0/2, 0,0; B 2/5/7/10,5,0; C 5/7/10/12,5,5; D 5/7/10/12,5,5; E 2/6/2/6,0,0; F 6/9/6/9,0,0; G 9/12/9/12,0,0; H 12/14/12/14,0,0; I 14/18/14/18,0,0; J 18/19/18/19,0,0. START occurs at 0, END at 19. If using total slack rather than free slack, B=5, C=5, D=5. The legend specifically asks for FREE slack: B free slack=0, C and D free slack=5. Accept topologically equivalent diagrams.
aiRubric: Inspect the DRAWING/UPLOADED IMAGE as primary evidence and award 2 marks for each of the 12 valid nodes: START, A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, I, J, END.
Credit each activity node's correct duration, placement, arrows/dependencies and correct earliest/latest date annotations; award proportionate partial marks when a node is partly right.
START→A, A→B,E; B→C,D; E→F→G; H must wait for C,D,G; H→I→J→END.
Correct forward pass ends at 19 weeks, using H ES=max(C EF7,D EF7,G EF12)=12.
Correct backward pass: B has total slack 5; C and D have total and free slack 5 each.
Figure 2 explicitly labels FREE SLACK at the bottom of each box: B's FREE slack is 0 despite B's TOTAL slack being 5.
Accept equivalent drawing arrangements and labelled time values; do not award full diagram/layout marks for unillustrated claims in an optional text box.
questions.aiReferenceNotes: This is a 24-mark visual marking question. Judge the actual submitted network and node labels as drawn. Table 4 specifies all precedence and duration data. Figure 2 node slots are ES, EF, activity/duration, LS, FREE slack, LF. Total slack B,C,D=5,5,5; FREE slack B,C,D=0,5,5. The critical path is A–E–F–G–H–I–J lasting 19 weeks. Do not apply the October/November 2021 paper's specific 7-of-14 missing-diagram deduction to this separate January/February 2025 paper.
